title: Software
text:
Tools I have written or contributed to for analysing bacterial growth — in plate readers, microfluidic chambers and bioreactors. Everything linked here is on GitHub.







FriendChip



Python

image analysis

microfluidics

author



Config-first Python pipeline for microfluidics timelapse image analysis — from raw Leica .lif and Nikon .nd2 files through segmentation, tracking and lineage reconstruction to growth rates, dose–response curves and spatial cross-feeding analytics. Omnipose segmentation with GPU acceleration; one JSON config per experiment, one CLI and web app to drive every stage.









plate-functions



R

growth curves

plate reader

author



R functions for 96-well plate-reader growth curves: log-linear sliding-window maximum growth rate, per-well yield / AUC / lag / carrying capacity, blank correction, time-grid sanity checks and per-plate parameter diagnostics. Shared as a git submodule across several lab projects.









ChiBio (fork)



Python

bioreactor

hardware

contributor



Fork of the open-source ChiBio bioreactor platform with additions for OD dilution-series calibration, timed dosing schedules, fluorescence-assisted OD control and measurement-mutex fixes for the device’s read/write sequences.

title: Constantinos Xenophontos
text:
I am a microbial ecologist working as a postdoctoral researcher in Gabriele Micali’s Microbial Ecology Lab at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital in Milan. I study how bacteria grow and interact — how cross-feeding, cooperation and cheating shape the composition of small communities, and how those interactions change the way populations respond to antibiotics.
My work sits between the bench and the terminal: I run growth experiments in plate readers, microfluidic chambers and continuous-culture bioreactors, and I write the analysis pipelines that turn those time-series into growth rates, lineages and dose–response curves. Most of that code is open — see Software.
I did my doctoral research in microbial ecology at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv), where I tested ecological theory with synthetic bacterial communities and models of public-goods “cheating”. Before that I trained in ecology and evolution at Imperial College London and in biology at the University of Hull.
